response.public_summary: Your parity logic is almost right but misses an edge case.

approach.student_idea_public: Check if `w` is even to decide `YES`.
approach.correct_idea_family: parity check with minimum sum constraint

suspect_inputs.why: smallest even cannot split into two positive evens

response.root_cause_internal: L6 only checks `w % 2 == 0`. Problem requires two parts each positive even, so each >=2 and sum >=4. w=2 is even but cannot be split into two positive evens. Condition missing `w>2` causes WA on that edge case.
response.fix_internal: Change L6 condition from `w % 2 == 0` to `w % 2 == 0 && w > 2` (or `w >= 4`). Both parts must be positive even, so each >=2, sum >=4.
response.checked_internal: Checked sample w=8 gives YES correct. Checked odd w gives NO correct. Checked minimal even w=2: needs two positive even parts, impossible, but code returns YES. No overflow or TLE issues.
